2 2. The brief facts of case is as under:
That on 12.05.2015 at about 6.45 a.m. Tony Mathew was proceeding in a Hyundai Eone Car bearing Reg.No.KL599607 along with his wife and father, which is belonging to R3 at Basavanapura, Ramanagara, B.M.Road, a Volvo Bus bearing Reg.No.KA09F4820 came in rash and negligent manner and dashed violently against said car from opposite direction, as a result, occupants of the said car have seriously injured, immediately they were shifted to Government Hospital, but Tony Mathew and his wife Rinu were died by the time they reached hospital, petitioner No.1/who is father of the deceased has sustained multiple fractures and was hospitalized.
Petitioners have shifted the dead body to their native by spending Rs.50,000/ towards transportation.
SCCH5 3.

At the time of accident, deceased/Tony Mathew was aged about 25 years, hale and healthy, he was working as Human Resource Executive in Sparsh Hospital Bengaluru, thereby earning Rs.30,000/
p.m. Petitioner No.1 is father, petitioner No.2 is mother of the deceased Tony Mathew, due to the death of the deceased, they have lost their life supporter and bread winner of the family.
Further they have put to great mental agony, hardship, their hopes have been totally destroyed and shattered.

Out of this accident crime No.80/2015 is registered before the Ramanagara P.S. R1 is the R.C.Owner of Volvo bus bearing Reg.No.KA09F4820, R2 is insurer and R3 is owner of Hyundai Eone Car bearing Reg.No.KL599607, R4 is driver of the bus bearing Reg.No.KA09F4820, R5 is insurer of the bus SCCH5 bearing Reg.No.KA09F4820, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.

Hence, prays to allow the petition and grant compensation of Rs.1,00,00,000/ with interest at the rate of 18% p.a.
4.
On service of notice, R1/ R.C.Owner of bus bearing Reg.No.KA09F4820 appeared and filed written statement denying case of the petitioners.
He has denied that petitioners are legal representatives of the deceased and depending on the income of the deceased.

Further submitted that, driver of the bus bearing Reg.No.KA09 F4820 was moving slowly, carefully and cautiously following traffic rules and regulations, so that, there is no negligency of the bus driver.
Further denied occupation and income of the deceased.
He has taken policy for the bus bearing Reg.No.KA 09F4820 vide policy certificate SCCH5 No.67210031140100003382 for the period from 30.03.2015 to 29.03.2016 from R5.
Claim made by the petitioner is higher side, hence his petition is not maintainable.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.

5. R2/insurer of the car bearing Reg.No.KL59 9607 appeared and filed written statement and admitted issuance of policy of insurance to the said car and his liability is subject to terms and conditions of the policy, further submitted that, deceased Tony Mathew himself was driving the Hyundai Eone Car, hence legal representatives of the deceased cannot maintain petition against the insurer of the said car.
Further submitted that, alleged accident is occurred due to negligency of the deceased himself.
Further submitted that, driver of the said car was not holding valid and effective driving SCCH5 license as on the date of accident.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.

6. R4 being the driver of the bus has remained absent, hence placed exparte.

R5/insurer of the bus has appeared and filed written statement by stating that, petition is filed under Sec.166 of M.V.Act for the death of Tony Mathew against whom the charge sheet is filed, so that, petition is not maintainable.

Further Ramanagar Traffic P.S. have filed charge sheet against the deceased in Cr.No.80/2015 for the offences punishable under Sec. 279, 304(A), 338 of IPC, so that, petitioners being the legal representatives of the deceased are not entitled for any compensation.
Deceased himself is tort feasor and SCCH5 responsible for his own death, claim made by the petitioners is higher side, hence their petition is not maintainable.
Further submitted that, driver of the Hyundai Eone Car was not having valid and effective driving license at the time of accident, further said car was not having fitness certificate.
Further submitted that, hospital authorities have not issued wound certificate.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.

2.
Whether petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?
3. What order or award?

9. Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record.

Then my findings on the above issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1 : In the Negative  Issue No.2 : In the Negative  Issue No.3 : As per final order for the  following:

10. Issue No.1: In order to prove her case, petitioner No.1/father of the deceased has deposed his evidence as PW1, in his chiefexamination he has reiterated the facts narrated in their petition.

In this regard copy of FIR is marked as Ex.P.1, copy of charge sheet is marked as Ex.P.2, copy of inquest is marked as SCCH5 Ex.P.3, copy of statement of witness is marked as Ex.P.4, copy of sketch is marked as Ex.P.5, copy of P.M.Report is marked as Ex.P.6, copy of IMV Report is marked as Ex.P.8, copy of Sec.133 notice is marked as Ex.P.9.
copy of complaint is marked as Ex.P.10, copy of crime detail form is marked as Ex.P.11.

11. In crossexamination by counsel for R1, there is no about place, date and time of the accident,
further stated that, on the day of the incident he was sitting on back seat of the car bearing Reg.No.KL599607, his son Tony Mathew had been driving the car, this accident is occurred nearby Ramanagar, on Mysore - Bengaluru Road.
Further denied that, very accident is occurred due to negligency of his son.
The witness volunteers that, very accident is occurred due to negligency of the bus driver, SCCH5 again admitted that, due to negligency of his son, this accident is occurred.
after investigation charge sheet is filed against his son, he has not given statement before the police.
Further denied that, he has given statement before the police stating that, very accident is occurred due to negligency of his son.
Further admits that, as per Ex.P.5 police have prepared hand sketch map and which is proper and correct.
Further deposed that, his son had driving licence to drive the car.
12. In crossexamination by counsel for R5 deposed that, his son had driving licence, at the time of accident his son had been driving the car.

Further admits that, as per the charge sheet, his son had driven the car rash and negligently, crossed the road divider and dashed against the KSRTC Volvo Bus, police have not SCCH5 recorded his statement.
Further he do not know that the charge sheet is filed against his son, he cannot say that who is owner of the car.
Further admits that, it is a personal car and not a taxi.
Further stated that, he do not know about violation of the registration conditions.

Further denied that, very petition is not maintainable under Sec.166 of M.V.Act.
13.

This accident is occurred while coming to Bengaluru from Kannur in Kerala State through Mysore Road, this accident is occurred on Mysuru  Bengaluru road, he do not know how this accident is occurred, he do not know that, their car jumped the divider on right side, then dashed against a bus which was coming on front side, at the time of accident he was sleeping, his SCCH5 son had been driving the car, he cannot say that, very accident is o cured due to negligency of his son.

14. In crossexamination by counsel for R2 deposed that, his son had been driving the car which was taken on rental basis, he do not know that, police have filed charge sheet against his son stating that, due to negligency of his son this accident is occurred, he do not know the contents of charge sheet.

Further denied that, they are not entitled for compensation;
15.
On going through the FIR and charge sheet it is noticed that, very crime No.80/2015
is registered before the Ramanagar P.S. against the driver of the car bearing Reg.No.KL59J9607.

Looking to the same, it is noticed that, in the morning hours deceased Tony Mathew has driven his car in high speed rash and negligently, crossed the divider, and dashed against a Volvo bus,
which was moving towards Maysore from Bengaluru on other side of the road.

Considering the same, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, very accident is occurred only due to negligency of the deceased, but as per the averments of the petition and chiefexamination of the PW1 there is negligency of the bus driver, said fact is not proved by him.
Hence I have answered Issue No.1 in the negative.
19. Issue No.2:
Very petition is filed against R1 to R5 for the relief of compensation under Sec.166 of M.V.Act, 1988.
In the case on hand, deceased is the tort SCCH5 feasor, he was driver of the car bearing Reg.No.KL59J 9607 at the time of accident, due to his own negligency very accident is occurred.
In this regard, findings are given on the above issue No.1.

Respondent No.1 is Managing Director of the KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No. KA09F4820, respondent No.4 is the driver of the said bus, respondent No.5 is insurer of the said bus, respondent No.3 is owner of the car bearing Reg.No. KL 59J9607, respondent no.2 is insurer of the said car.
When petition is filed under Sec.166 of M.V.Act, under such circumstances, negligency of the bus driver shall be proved, but in the case on hand, negligency of the bus driver is not proved.
Under such circumstances, petition under Sec.166 of M.V.Act is not maintainable.
SCCH5 20.

Very car is standing in the name of R3, it is a personal car of the R3, having white board, which can be used only for his personal purposes, but as per say of the PW1 in his crossexamination very car was taken on rental basis, but not produced any documents.
It goes to show that, son of the petitioners has used car of the R3 for his personal use.
Under such circumstances, definitely he can step into the shoes of the owner at the time of driving the car, if there is package policy or own damage policy.
21. In the case on hand, legal manager of the respondent No.2/car insurer has deposed her evidence as RW1 and furnished policy pertains to the car and marked at Ex.R.2.
On perusal of the policy it is noticed that, very policy was in force since 21.07.2014 to SCCH5 20.07.2015, very accident is occurred on 12.05.2015.
Under such circumstances it is clear that, policy issued by the R2 was in force in favour of the said car at the time of accident.

Very policy is a package policy, under such circumstances, it petition is filed under Sec.163(a) of the M.V.Act, petitioners would have been entitled for some compensation, but in the case on hand, very petition is filed under Sec.166 of M.V.Act.
Under such circumstances, very petition is not maintainable.
22. Further R5 has deposed her evidence as per RW2 furnished and marked the copy of policy pertains to bus bearing Reg.No.KA09F4820 marked at Ex.R.4.
On perusal of the same it is noticed that, very policy is a package policy, having validity since 30.03.2015 to 29.03.2016, very accident is occurred on 12.05.2015.

under such circumstances, it is clear that, very policy was in force at the time of accident,
but there is no negligency on the part of bus driver.
Under such circumstances, petitioners are not entitled for compensation from respondent No.1, 4 and 5.
For all these reasons, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, very petition is not maintainable.

23. During argument filing of the petition under wrong provisions of the law is brought to notice of the counsel for petitioner, but he has not taken any steps to amend the petition and take necessary steps.
So that, petitioners are not entitled for compensation under Sec.166 of M.V.Act.

When very petition is not maintainable, under such circumstances, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, it is not necessary to SCCH5 discuss about the age and income of the deceased, entitlement of compensation by the petitioners.
I have answered Issue No.2 in the negative.
24. Issue No.3:

Inview of the above reasoning and discussions to the above issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
::ORDER::
The petition filed by the Petitioners under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is hereby dismissed Parties have to bear their own costs.
Draw award accordingly.
